decision.summaryForCoordinator: The corpus holds up under byte-level checking. All eight catalogued fixtures exist, all eight digests reproduce by recomputation at both ends of the review, all eight files are 0444, and the eight paths are distinct under casefold — as are all eighteen when combined with the sibling FX-1 catalog and as are the eighteen filenames on disk. The omit semantics are exactly right, checked three ways per member: each token list equals the catalog's permissionsDeclared as an ordered comparison, each set difference against v9's live seven equals the catalog's omitted list, and each omitted token is absent from its file. Seven omit-exactly-one members omit seven distinct tokens covering the closed set once each, and omit-all carries a genuinely empty permissions array. This reviewer treated the uniform 2740-byte size of the seven omit files as a possible sign they were identical and resolved it: a field-by-field diff shows only name and permissions differ, and the constancy is arithmetic, since the name grows by the omitted token's length exactly as the removed array entry shrinks. PR-1 is the correct class — v9 defines it as token-not-declared, absence denies. The fixtures carry v11's typed-null reserved markers verbatim and v11's {permission, reason} shape. No refusal-record or journal bytes appear anywhere, and the stated reason — that those envelopes are unspecified — is true on live bytes, where 'envelope', 'recordShape', 'wire format' and 'frame shape' all occur zero times while v9 names only the record kinds and their ordering. Custody is clean: subject unmoved at a7226e4b and 0444, four of four cited digests equal live bytes, file 08 pin equal to live and unmodified, HEAD 5d5d778, required-now 26, thirty gate rows, and neither QUALIFIED nor SATISFIED occurs anywhere in the subject. Seventeen attacks run, seventeen refuted, zero findings. One observation is positive: the eight FX-2A files this reviewer flagged as uncatalogued at the FX-1 review are now catalogued, and the pinned directory has no uncatalogued file left.
